terms.gloss: a garland of flowers, laid as an offering
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 385–386: corōnās flōreās: haec impōnentur in focō nostrō Larī
terms.comment: What a Roman household laid on the hearth for its Lar: in Plautus the god of the house says that the daughter honours him every day with incense or wine and gives him garlands, and her father buys flower garlands for him before her wedding. Cato bids the farm manager’s wife put a garland on the hearth on feast days. For an offering of any kind, dōnum.

terms.gloss: a gift; to a god, an offering
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. dōnum: “a present brought to a deity, a votive offering”

phrases.latin: nunc tūsculum ēmī hoc et corōnās flōreās: haec impōnentur in focō nostrō Larī, ut fortūnātās faciat gnātae nūptiās.
phrases.english: Now I’ve bought this bit of incense and some flower garlands: they’ll be laid on our hearth for the Lar, so that he may make my daughter’s wedding a happy one.

phrases.latin: Kal., Īdibus, Nōnīs, fēstus diēs cum erit, corōnam in focum indat
phrases.english: on the Kalends, the Ides, and the Nones, and whenever there is a feast day, she is to put a garland on the hearth
Mind you don’t step on the offerings!

phrases.latin: Mulier flōrēs, orȳzam, tūs in līmine pōnit, dōnum deīs.
phrases.english: The woman sets flowers, rice, and incense on the doorstep, an offering to the gods.

sources: Lewis & Short: floreus · Lewis & Short: corona · Lewis & Short: donum
